findings.text: Filesystem mark creation validates absolute pathname form without trailing separator, obtains parent and child identity either by lookup or from supplied context, allocates a mark bound to the audit notification group with the audit event mask and owning rule, snapshots device and inode identity with unset fallback, and registers on the parent directory while reporting validation lookup memory or registration failures.

Watch subtree and inode attachment helpers enforce exclusivity before linking, limiting watch and subtree forms to exit family lists with equality comparison and permitting equality plus inequality for inode form, and report invalid combinations memory shortage or unsupported configuration including compile time fallback errors.

Watch and subtree registration resolve filesystem locations outside the filter critical section and link under protection, sharing an existing parent or tree on pathname identity match and otherwise publishing a new object, with inode hash bucket selection for watches and mount tagging plus chunk activation for subtrees.

Rule translation and installation pipeline builds a blank entry from list selector action flags masks and field count with class expansion, converts each field operator and value with type specific handling for identity security path key and executable forms, validates list operator and value combinations, then performs duplicate search priority assignment and ordered insertion with signal accounting.

Path based selectors require absolute text without trailing separator, allow at most one filesystem attachment of watch subtree inode or executable kind per rule, and restrict watch subtree and inode selectors to exit family lists.

Field validity is a joint function of selector list comparison operator and value, with message type limited to exclude and user lists, filesystem type limited to filesystem list, permission checks rejected for uring exit, filesystem list accepting only type and key, string like executable key watch directory archival and related selectors limited to equality forms, several numeric identity selectors rejecting bit test forms, and bounds on permission bits file type bits address family compare index and boolean login set values.

Unset login identity is normalized to a dedicated set selector with zero value plus a legacy flag, filter key and executable attachment each allow at most one instance per rule under length caps, string payload lengths accumulate toward rule buffer accounting, and an inode inequality selector is discarded after translation.
External operator codes map to internal ordering by linear search from equality up to a bad sentinel, with unknown codes yielding the sentinel and later rejected during field validation.

Duplicate detection compares full rule content within a scope chosen by attachment kind, using one inode hash bucket for inode rules, full hash scan for watch rules whose inode is not yet known, and per list chain otherwise.

Exit family rules receive monotonic priority increasing for prepend and decreasing otherwise while other rules retain maximal value, prepend selects head versus tail insertion on both the ordered registry and the read copy update list before the flag is cleared, and user exclude and filesystem lists are excluded from syscall rule counting.

Signal coverage uses architecture classification to select native versus compat signal class masks, requires both when architecture is absent, treats unknown architecture as covered, and reports uncovered only when no mask word intersects the class definition.
Parent resolution refreshes watch device and inode identity only when the resolved child exists and otherwise preserves prior values, always releasing lookup references.

Filter mutex guards duplicate search registry insertion parent linkage and tree publication, is temporarily released around parent pathname lookup and around subtree path collection plus mount tagging with reacquisition before linking, while a separate hash spin guard protects chunk marker updates and parent linkage asserts mutex ownership.

Rule object aggregates list selector action flags priority field count syscall masks field array cached arch and inode references optional filter key executable mark watch subtree and temporary tree pointers buffer length accounting plus ordered registry linkage hash linkage and per parent or per tree membership linkage.

Filesystem attachment objects carry pathname ownership device and inode identity with unset sentinels reference counts and rule membership lists, with watches adding parent and sibling linkage, subtrees adding tombstone state root pointer and chunk global and same root lists, executable marks adding event masked notification state and owning rule back reference, and parents adding masked notification state and watch list.

Subtree registration moves from seed allocation through global pathname match to sharing or publication, then prune thread assurance path resolution mount tagging and chunk activation, committing the rule tree pointer only if membership survives reclamation and otherwise detaching global and rule links and releasing the seed.

Watch registration moves from temporary watch allocation through reference retention and mutex release to parent lookup, then under mutex to parent discovery or creation with pathname based sharing that transfers rule ownership to the surviving watch and adjusts references, followed by rule membership linking and hash bucket selection.

Failure handling unwinds partial state through encoded errors, releasing temporary subtree executable and entry allocations on translation failure, releasing seed or extra watch references on duplicate or lookup failure, freeing unlinked parents only when empty, and substituting compile time error stubs when filesystem auditing is unavailable.
Prune thread startup is attempted at most once with an existing instance treated as success and creation failure reported as memory shortage after clearing the handle.
Security string rules tolerate currently invalid policy values by warning and retaining the field for possible future policy reload while other initialization failures abort rule construction.

Fragments distinguish symbolic filter list selectors action selectors comparison operators permission file type address family and field compare bounds pathname and key length caps syscall mask geometry inode bucket count event masks and unset device and inode sentinels without exposing numeric encodings.
